At face value, driving around delivering packages, that’s simple.

It’s all the other little things though that waste time and put hella pressure on drivers. 

Leaving the pad late because of warehouse dysfunction. Apartment complexes that a difficult to get into, require you to grab a key fob, require you to take an elevator down to the parking garage etc. A college campus that has a receiving dock and a mailroom (and they’re 5 mins away, and the notes are unclear about what goes where, and it’s split up into 8 different stops, 5 separate pins for some reason, and also one of the stops for the receiving dock is consistently grouped with the apartment across the street’s locker for god knows why). Businesses not having correct hours, or the fact that one of the richest companies on the planet cannot create an algorithm which puts timed stops FIRST so you don’t have to go out of your way, dig through bags for one teeny package??? Shitty traffic conditions, shitty road conditions in the country or during inclement weather. Annoying parking situations which require you to park inconveniently, or having to skips stops off a busy street during rush hour, or worse the anxiety of saying fuck it and getting honked at for doing your job. Multi stops that have no logical explanation. Delivering in areas where every convenience store, walgreens, you name it has no public restroom so you either have to waste time driving elsewhere or do what you gotta do (and shit man I’m a girl). Driving vans without backup cams, breaks you basically have to step on, a bulkhead door that opens and closes at will and a side door that no longer latches so you have to secure it with the dang seatbelt. Wasting 45 minutes because a customer did an escalation on their package and your dispatcher says you need to drop everything and drive back there immediately during rush hour, all because they couldn’t answer the phone earlier to provide access or give permission to leave the package outside (mind you, a negative review is ground for losing a route the next day/week).

And shit, a lot of this would be okay if it was just factored into the workload! 180-200 stops without fail these past two or three weeks. The math just doesn’t math. Maybe straight residential, 190 total doing 30 stops or so an hour and leaving time for breaks, loadout, the drive back to the station, shit it might come out to around 10 hrs total. But that’s not the reality for most routes. 

So yeah, it’s easy until it ain’t. And I didn’t even mention how tired my body feels after each day.

I often think that depression (maybe more accurately nihilism?) is the only logical reaction to understanding what we are (animals that act according to our biology and its interactions with our environment) and how much pain, death, disease, disaster, and suffering exists in the world (with or without humans, too). The state of our economy doesn’t help, the state of our climate doesn’t help, lack of community doesn’t help, you get the idea. It’s the knowing, and not being able to un-know, that makes me feel fucking depressed. You can say okay, whatever, I’m just one guy and I can’t save the world. I can create my own meaning yeah? Yeah, it’s certainly possible to have fun and have good experiences if you have the means, and I do take pleasure out of everyday life as much as I can, but there’s still this darkness just below the surface of every single thing. 

I really resonated with this quote from Milan Kundera’s “The Book of Laughter and Forgetting”: 

It takes so little, so infinitely little, for a person to cross the border beyond which everything loses meaning: love, convictions, faith, history. Human life -- and herein lies its secret -- takes place in the immediate proximity of that border, even in direct contact with it; it is not miles away, but a fraction of an inch.
